title: DevForgeAI stack.yaml section
description: One anchored section of .devforgeai/stack.yaml. The file itself is a mapping of anchor name to a document of this shape; a story's commands.source names one anchor and pins the whole file by hash. This is the only place a literal build, test, lint or format command exists. No worker ever receives one: a phase names a command key and the sequencer resolves and runs it inside the transition oracle.

compiled.description: true when the stack needs a build before its tests can run. commands.build is then mandatory and the oracle runs it before test on every transition.

manifests.description: Dependency manifests. Only files matching one of these are scanned against packages.allow and packages.deny.

commands.description: The closed command-key set. A phase may run only the keys its registry entry grants and the run's commands.use authorises.

ignore_dirs.description: Optional; defaults to an empty list. Root-relative directories that are build or cache output rather than source: excluded when the sequencer copies the project tree into a copy-mode candidate root, excluded from the tree-hash manifest that copy mode uses as base_ref and as each checkpoint, and ignored by the mutation check on a brokered command, which would otherwise read a compiler's own output as an undeclared write. A directory listed here is never promoted and never rewound.

junit_dialect.description: Optional; defaults to generic. Which runner wrote junit_path, so the oracle can read that runner's JUnit faithfully instead of guessing. generic trusts the file literally: a <failure> is a test failure and an <error> is an import or collection error. pytest and node name runners that encode both outcomes in the same element, and the oracle normalises them before classification: a non-assertion throw is COLLECTION_ERROR, not a satisfied red gate, and a file whose tests never ran is NO_TESTS, not a pass. Naming the wrong dialect weakens no gate; it only reads a runner's own vocabulary less precisely.

runner_probe.description: A cheap liveness check for the runner. A probe that does not return exit_ok is reason_code runner_missing, never a phase failure.

allow.description: Exact package names, compared case-insensitively against every name an extractor captures. An empty list disables the allowlist check.

deny.description: Regular expressions matched against manifest text. Any match is a refusal.

extractors.description: How package names are read out of each manifest syntax. A dependency no extractor recognises is not enforced.

forbidden_imports.description: Source-level bans, scanned on proposed content before application and over the whole tree at every transition.

argv.description: An exec-form argument vector. It is launched without a shell; no redirect, pipeline, substitution or variable is interpreted.

cwd.description: Repository-relative working directory. Defaults to the project root.

junit_path.description: Where the runner writes its JUnit XML. Mandatory on the test key: the oracle reads per-test outcomes from this file, not from stdout.

timeout_s.description: Wall-clock limit. Defaults to 600. Exceeding it is classification TIMEOUT and reason_code timeout.

paths.description: Which manifests this extractor reads. Defaults to the section's manifests.

regex.description: Multiline regular expression whose capture group 1 is the package name. An extractor without a capture group is a policy error, not a silent pass.

reason.description: The constitution anchor this ban enforces. It is quoted verbatim in the refusal.
